newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close mixed, pork bellies mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close mixed, pork bellies mostly lower.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mixed with nearbys higher on late commercial support while pork belly futures remained mostly lower despite paring of losses late, traders said.

Hog futures were underpinned much of the day by steadier- than-projected cash hog prices Tuesday and a strong tone to pork prices. Packers raised bids early Tuesday to encourage hog marketings and stronger pork markets likely widened packer margins, traders said.
The grade two estimated gross pork cutout value quoted Monday was the highest since October 13, sources noted.

Rand Financials bought and locals covered short positions in December at the close. Rand had been on both sides of the market earlier. Spreaders bought December and sold February and April late after buying February and selling April early. Cargill Investor Services bought February and sold December early, pit sources said.

In hog options, a local sold December 56 puts while commission houses sold December 58 calls. Futures traders bought December 60 calls, traders said. Late in the day, Smith-Barney bought December 58 puts, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures ranged on both sides of previous levels with stronger cash belly prices providing early support while a technical adjustment from an oversold condition weighed on the market. Futures appeared to have made the technical adjustment when prices tumbled around midday because the market rallied late on local and fund buying and buy stops to close with pared gains, traders said.

Fundamental support came from 14-16 lb cash belly prices which ranged up to $71 per cwt, the highest price since October 8. The recent light slaughter pace and overall light fresh belly storings reinforced support, they said.
After the close, the CME reported last week's out-of-town net storage movement at in 2.245 million lbs, in the range of analyst estimates of in 1.25 to 2.5 million lbs.
Hogs closed up 0.250 cent a lb to off 0.200 with December up most at 58.500 cents. Bellies ended up 0.125 to off 1.100 with February off 0.250 at 76.625 cents.
